public_domain_references.bsb: But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this, they were deeply disturbed that someone had come to seek the well-being of the Israelites.
public_domain_references.web: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite servant heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly, because a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
public_domain_references.asv: And when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly, for that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard [of it], it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Sanaballat the Aronite heard [it], and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and it was grievous to them that a man was come to seek good for the children of Israel.

pob.text: So I came to Jerusalem and was there three days.

spob.text: So I arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.

public_domain_references.bsb: After I had arrived in Jerusalem and had been there three days,
public_domain_references.web: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
public_domain_references.asv: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
public_domain_references.kjv: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.
public_domain_references.brenton: So I came to Jerusalem, and was there three days.

pob.text: So I arose in the night[a], I and a few men with me, and I had not told anyone what my God was putting into my heart to do for Jerusalem[c][b]. And there was no animal with me except the animal on which I was riding.

spob.text: So I got up during the night with a few men. I had not told anyone what my God was putting into my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one I was riding.

public_domain_references.bsb: I set out at night with a few men. I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one on which I was riding.
public_domain_references.web: I arose in the night, I and a few men with me. I didn’t tell anyone what my God put into my heart to do for Jerusalem. There wasn’t any animal with me except the animal that I rode on.
public_domain_references.asv: And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I any man what my God put into my heart to do for Jerusalem; neither was there any beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And I arose in the night, I and some few men with me; neither told I [any] man what my God had put in my heart to do at Jerusalem: neither [was there any] beast with me, save the beast that I rode upon.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I rose up by night, I and a few men with me; and I told no man what God put into my heart to do with Israel; and there was no beast with me, except the beast which I rode upon.

pob.text: So I went out by night through the Valley Gate[a], toward the Dragon Spring and toward the Dung Gate[b], and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and its gates that had been consumed by fire.

spob.text: So that night I went out through the Valley Gate. I traveled toward the Dragon Spring[a] and the Dung Gate, inspecting[b] Jerusalem’s walls along the way. The walls had been broken down, and fire had consumed the city’s gates.

public_domain_references.bsb: So I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward the Well of the Serpent and the Dung Gate, and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and the gates that had been destroyed by fire.
public_domain_references.web: I went out by night by the valley gate toward the jackal’s well, then to the dung gate; and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and its gates were consumed with fire.
public_domain_references.asv: And I went out by night by the valley gate, even toward the jackal’s well, and to the dung gate, and viewed the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and the gates thereof were consumed with fire.
public_domain_references.kjv: And I went out by night by the gate of the valley, even before the dragon well, and to the dung port, and viewed the walls of Jerusalem, which were broken down, and the gates thereof were consumed with fire.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I went forth by the gate of the valley by night, and to the mouth of the well of fig trees, and to the dung-gate: and I mourned over the wall of Jerusalem which they were destroying, and her gates were devoured with fire.

pob.text: Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and to the King’s Pool[b][a], but there was no place for the animal under me to pass.

spob.text: Then I continued to the Fountain Gate[a] and the King’s Pool, but there was not enough room for the animal I was riding to get through.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King’s Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to get through;
public_domain_references.web: Then I went on to the spring gate and to the king’s pool, but there was no place for the animal that was under me to pass.
public_domain_references.asv: Then I went on to the fountain gate and to the king’s pool: but there was no place for the beast that was under me to pass.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then I went on to the gate of the fountain, and to the king’s pool: but [there was] no place for the beast [that was] under me to pass.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I passed on to the fountain gate, and to the king's pool; and there was no room for the beast to pass under me.

pob.text: So I went up by the wadi at night and inspected the wall[a]. Then I turned back and entered by the Valley Gate[b], and returned.

spob.text: That night I went up along the ravine and inspected the wall.[a] Then I turned back, entered through the Valley Gate, and returned.

public_domain_references.bsb: so I went up the valley by night and inspected the wall. Then I headed back and reentered through the Valley Gate.
public_domain_references.web: Then I went up in the night by the brook and inspected the wall; and I turned back, and entered by the valley gate, and so returned.
public_domain_references.asv: Then went I up in the night by the brook, and viewed the wall; and I turned back, and entered by the valley gate, and so returned.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then went I up in the night by the brook, and viewed the wall, and turned back, and entered by the gate of the valley, and [so] returned.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I went up by the wall of the brook by night, and mourned over the wall, and passed through the gate of the valley, and returned.

pob.text: But the officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing[a], and until then I had not told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or the rest who were doing the work.

spob.text: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing. Until then, I had not told the Jews,[a] the priests, the nobles, the officials, or anyone else doing the work.

public_domain_references.bsb: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews or priests or nobles or officials or any other workers.
public_domain_references.web: The rulers didn’t know where I went, or what I did. I had not as yet told it to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest who did the work.
public_domain_references.asv: And the rulers knew not whither I went, or what I did; neither had I as yet told it to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest that did the work.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the rulers knew not whither I went, or what I did; neither had I as yet told [it] to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the rulers, nor to the rest that did the work.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the sentinels knew not why I went, nor what I was doing; and until that time I told [it] not to the Jews, or to the priests, or to the nobles, or to the captains, or to the rest [of the men] who wrought the works.

pob.text: Then I said to them[a], “You see the trouble we are in: Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem[c][b], so that we may no longer be a reproach.”

spob.text: Then I said to them, “You can see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild Jerusalem’s wall so that we will no longer be an object of scorn.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I said to them, “You see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned down. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”
public_domain_references.web: Then I said to them, “You see the bad situation that we are in, how Jerusalem lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire. Come, let’s build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we won’t be disgraced.”
public_domain_references.asv: Then said I unto them, Ye see the evil case that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we [are] in, how Jerusalem [lieth] waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then I said to them, Ye see this evil, in which we are, how Jerusalem is desolate, and her gates have been set on fire: come, and let us build throughout the wall of Jerusalem, and we shall be no longer a reproach.

pob.text: So I told them that the hand of my God was good upon me[a], and also the words of the king that he had spoken to me. And they said[c][b], “Let us rise up and build.” So they strengthened their hands for the good work.

spob.text: So I told them how my God’s hand had helped me. I also told them what the king had said to me. They replied, “Let us rise up and build!” Then they took courage and prepared themselves for the good work.

public_domain_references.bsb: I also told them about the gracious hand of my God upon me, and what the king had said to me. “Let us start rebuilding,” they replied, and they set their hands to this good work.
public_domain_references.web: I told them about the hand of my God which was good on me, and also about the king’s words that he had spoken to me. They said, “Let’s rise up and build.” So they strengthened their hands for the good work.
public_domain_references.asv: And I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me, as also of the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for the good [work].
public_domain_references.kjv: Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for [this] good [work].
public_domain_references.brenton: And I told them of the hand of God which was good upon me, also about the words of the king which he spoke to me: and I said, Let us arise and build. And their hands were strengthened for the good [work].

pob.text: But when Sanballat the Horonite[a], Tobiah the Ammonite slave, and Geshem the Arab heard, they mocked us and despised us, and said, “What is this thing that you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?”

spob.text: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite slave,[a] and Geshem the Arab heard, they mocked us and treated us with contempt. They asked, “What are you doing? Are you rebelling against the king?”

public_domain_references.bsb: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about this, they mocked us and ridiculed us, saying, “What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?”
public_domain_references.web: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they ridiculed us and despised us, and said, “What is this thing that you are doing? Will you rebel against the king?”
public_domain_references.asv: But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard it, they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?
public_domain_references.kjv: But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, heard [it], they laughed us to scorn, and despised us, and said, What [is] this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?
public_domain_references.brenton: And Sanaballat the Aronite, and Tobia the servant, the Ammonite, and Gesam the Arabian, heard [it], and they laughed us to scorn, and came to us, and said, What [is] this thing that ye are doing? are ye revolting against the king?

pob.text: Then I answered them and said[a], “The God of heaven, he will make us prosper, and we his servants will arise and build[b]. But you have no share or right or memorial in Jerusalem.”

spob.text: I replied, “The God of heaven will give us success, and we, his servants, will rise up and build. But you have no share in Jerusalem, no rightful claim there, and no memorial there.”

public_domain_references.bsb: So I answered them and said, “The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success. We, His servants, will start rebuilding, but you have no portion, right, or claim in Jerusalem.”
public_domain_references.web: Then I answered them, and said to them, “The God of heaven will prosper us. Therefore we, his servants, will arise and build; but you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial in Jerusalem.”
public_domain_references.asv: Then answered I them, and said unto them, The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then answered I them, and said unto them, The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I answered them, and said to them, The God of heaven, he shall prosper us, and we his servants are pure, and we will build: but ye have no part, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.

pob.text: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests[a], and they built the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set up its doors; they consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Tower of Hananel.

spob.text: Then Eliashib the high priest and his brothers, the priests, began the work. They built the Sheep Gate. They themselves consecrated it[a] and put its doors in place. They also consecrated the section extending from there to the Tower of the Hundred and on to the Tower of Hananel.

public_domain_references.bsb: At the Sheep Gate, Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests began rebuilding. They dedicated it and installed its doors. After building as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel, they dedicated the wall.
public_domain_references.web: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brothers the priests, and they built the sheep gate. They sanctified it, and set up its doors. They sanctified it even to the tower of Hammeah, to the tower of Hananel.
public_domain_references.asv: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brethren the priests, and they builded the sheep gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even unto the tower of Hammeah they sanctified it, unto the tower of Hananel.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then Eliashib the high priest rose up with his brethren the priests, and they builded the sheep gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even unto the tower of Meah they sanctified it, unto the tower of Hananeel.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then Eliasub the high priest, and his brethren the priests, rose up, and built the sheep-gate; they sanctified it, and set up the doors of it; even to the tower of the hundred they sanctified [it], to the tower of Anameel.

pob.text: And next to him the men of Jericho built[a], and next to them Zaccur the son of Imri built.

spob.text: The men of Jericho built beside him. Zaccur son of Imri built beside them.

public_domain_references.bsb: The men of Jericho built next to Eliashib, and Zaccur son of Imri built next to them.
public_domain_references.web: Next to him the men of Jericho built. Next to them Zaccur the son of Imri built.
public_domain_references.asv: And next unto him builded the men of Jericho. And next to them builded Zaccur the son of Imri.
public_domain_references.kjv: And next unto him builded the men of Jericho. And next to them builded Zaccur the son of Imri.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [they builded] by the side of the men of Jericho, and by the side of the sons of Zacchur, the son of Amari.

pob.text: The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate[a]; they roofed it and set up its doors, its bolts[b], and its bars.

spob.text: Hassenaah’s descendants[a] built the Fish Gate. They put a roof over it[b] and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Fish Gate was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah. They laid its beams and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
public_domain_references.web: The sons of Hassenaah built the fish gate. They laid its beams, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.
public_domain_references.asv: And the fish gate did the sons of Hassenaah build; they laid the beams thereof, and set up the doors thereof, the bolts thereof, and the bars thereof.
public_domain_references.kjv: But the fish gate did the sons of Hassenaah build, who [also] laid the beams thereof, and set up the doors thereof, the locks thereof, and the bars thereof.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the sons of Asana built the fish-gate; they roofed it, and covered in its doors, and bolts, and bars.

pob.text: And next to them Meremoth son of Uriah[a], son of Hakkoz, made repairs; and next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs[c][b]; and next to them Zadok son of Baana made repairs.

spob.text: Next to them, Meremoth son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz repaired part of the wall. Beside them, Meshullam son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel repaired another part. Next to them, Zadok son of Baana repaired another part.

public_domain_references.bsb: Next to them, Meremoth son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to him, Meshullam son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel, made repairs; and next to him, Zadok son of Baana made repairs as well.
public_domain_references.web: Next to them, Meremoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz made repairs. Next to them, Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel made repairs. Next to them, Zadok the son of Baana made repairs.
public_domain_references.asv: And next unto them repaired Meremoth the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz. And next unto them repaired Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel. And next unto them repaired Zadok the son of Baana.
public_domain_references.kjv: And next unto them repaired Meremoth the son of Urijah, the son of Koz. And next unto them repaired Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabeel. And next unto them repaired Zadok the son of Baana.

pob.text: And next to them the Tekoites made repairs[b][a], but their nobles would not put their necks to the work of their lords.

spob.text: Next to them, the men of Tekoa made repairs. But their leading men refused to take part in the work directed by their superiors.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Next to him, the Tekoites made repairs, but their nobles did not put their shoulders to the work under their supervisors.
public_domain_references.web: Next to them, the Tekoites made repairs; but their nobles didn’t put their necks to the Lord’s work.
public_domain_references.asv: And next unto them the Tekoites repaired; but their nobles put not their necks to the work of their lord.
public_domain_references.kjv: And next unto them the Tekoites repaired; but their nobles put not their necks to the work of their Lord.
public_domain_references.brenton: And next to them the Thecoim took [their] place; but the Adorim applied not their neck to their service.

pob.text: And Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate. They laid its beams and set up its doors[a], its bolts, and its bars.

pob.text: And next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite made repairs[a], along with the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, for the seat of the governor of the province Beyond the River.

spob.text: Next to them, Melatiah from Gibeon and Jadon from Meronoth repaired the wall together with men from Gibeon and Mizpah. Their work was for the official seat of the governor of the province called Beyond the River.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Next to them, repairs were made by Melatiah the Gibeonite, Jadon the Meronothite, and the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, who were under the authority of the governor of the region west of the Euphrates.

public_domain_references.asv: And next unto them repaired Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon, and of Mizpah, [that appertained] to the throne of the governor beyond the River.
public_domain_references.kjv: And next unto them repaired Melatiah the Gibeonite, and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon, and of Mizpah, unto the throne of the governor on this side the river.
public_domain_references.brenton: And next to them repaired Maltias the Gabaonite, and Evaron the Meronothite, the men of Gabaon and Maspha, to the throne of the governor on this side the river.

pob.text: Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah[a], one of the goldsmiths, made repairs; and next to him Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs. And they restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.

spob.text: Working next to him, Uzziel son of Harhaiah, a goldsmith, made repairs. Beside Uzziel, Hananiah, a perfumer, also made repairs. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.[a]

public_domain_references.web: Next to him, Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths, made repairs. Next to him, Hananiah, one of the perfumers, made repairs, and they fortified Jerusalem even to the wide wall.
public_domain_references.asv: Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths. And next unto him repaired Hananiah one of the perfumers, and they fortified Jerusalem even unto the broad wall.

pob.text: Next to them[a], Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.

pob.text: Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-moab repaired another section[b][a], and also the Tower of the Ovens.

pob.text: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate[a]. They built it and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall[c][b], as far as the Dung Gate.

pob.text: And Shallun son of Col-hozeh[a], official of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He rebuilt it and roofed it, and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king’s garden, as far as the stairs that go down from the City of David.

spob.text: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, an official of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate. He himself rebuilt it and put a roof on it. He also installed its doors, bolts, and bars. Then he repaired the wall beside the Pool of Shelah,[a] near the king’s garden, as far as the stairs that go down from the City of David.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Fountain Gate was repaired by Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah. He rebuilt it, roofed it, and installed its doors, bolts, and bars. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah near the king’s garden, as far as the stairs that descend from the City of David.
public_domain_references.web: Shallun the son of Colhozeh, the ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the spring gate. pob.text: After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk[a], ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, made repairs as far as opposite the tombs of David, and as far as the pool that was made[b], and as far as the house of the mighty men.

spob.text: After him,[a] Nehemiah son of Azbuk made repairs. He ruled half the district of Beth-zur. His work extended to the point across from David’s tombs, to the man-made pool, and to the mighty men’s building.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Beyond him, Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of a half-district of Beth-zur, made repairs up to a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the artificial pool and the House of the Mighty.

public_domain_references.kjv: After him repaired Nehemiah the son of Azbuk, the ruler of the half part of Beth-zur, unto [the place] over against the sepulchres of David, and to the pool that was made, and unto the house of the mighty.
public_domain_references.brenton: After him repaired Neemias son of Azabuch, ruler of half the district round about Bethsur, as far as the garden of David's sepulchre, and as far as the artificial pool, and as far as the house of the mighty men.

pob.text: When Sanballat and Tobiah and the Arabs and the Ammonites and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of Jerusalem’s walls had gone up[a], that the breaches had begun to be closed[b], they became very angry.

spob.text: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repair work on Jerusalem’s walls was moving forward and that the broken places in the walls were beginning to be closed, they became very angry.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and filled with indignation. He ridiculed the Jews
public_domain_references.web: But when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was angry, and was very indignant, and mocked the Jews.
public_domain_references.asv: But it came to pass that, when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked the Jews.
public_domain_references.kjv: But it came to pass, that when Sanballat heard that we builded the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked the Jews.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now it came to pass, when Sanaballat heard that we were building the wall, that it was grievous to him, and he was very angry, and railed against the Jews.

pob.text: And all of them conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and to cause confusion in it[a].

spob.text: They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw the city into confusion.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: before his associates and the army of Samaria, saying, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Can they restore the wall by themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they complete it in a day? Can they bring these burnt stones back to life from the mounds of rubble?”
public_domain_references.web: He spoke before his brothers and the army of Samaria, and said, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they fortify themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive the stones out of the heaps of rubbish, since they are burned?”
public_domain_references.asv: And he spake before his brethren and the army of Samaria, and said, What are these feeble Jews doing? will they fortify themselves? will they sacrifice? will they make an end in a day? will they revive the stones out of the heaps of rubbish, seeing they are burned?
public_domain_references.kjv: And he spake before his brethren and the army of Samaria, and said, What do these feeble Jews? will they fortify themselves? will they sacrifice? will they make an end in a day? will they revive the stones out of the heaps of the rubbish which are burned?
public_domain_references.brenton: And he said before his brethren (that [is] the army of the Samaritans) [Is it true] that these Jews are building their city? do they indeed offer sacrifices? will they prevail? and will they this day restore the stones, after they have been burnt and made a heap of rubbish?

pob.text: So we prayed to our God and stationed a guard against them day and night because of them[a][b].

spob.text: So we prayed to our God. We also posted guards against them day and night because of the danger they posed.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Tobiah the Ammonite, who was beside him, said, “If even a fox were to climb up on what they are building, it would break down their wall of stones!”

public_domain_references.brenton: And Tobias the Ammanite came near to him, and said to them, Do they sacrifice or eat in their place? shall not a fox go up and pull down their wall of stones?

pob.text: And Judah said[a], “The strength of the burden-bearers has failed, and there is much rubble[b], and we are not able to build the wall.”

spob.text: The people of Judah said, “The workers carrying the loads have lost their strength. There is so much rubble, and we cannot build the wall.”

pob.text: And our adversaries said[a], “They will not know, and they will not see, until we come into their midst and kill them and stop the work.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Do not cover up their iniquity or let their sin be blotted out from Your sight, for they have provoked the builders.

pob.text: And when the Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times[a], “From all the places where you turn[b], they will come up against us,”

spob.text: Then the Jews who lived near the enemies came and warned us ten times, “Wherever you turn,[a] they will attack us from every direction.”

public_domain_references.bsb: So we rebuilt the wall until all of it was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.
public_domain_references.web: So we built the wall; and all the wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.

spob.text: Then I posted men at the lowest places behind the wall, in the exposed areas.[a] I stationed the people by families, carrying their swords, spears, and bows.

pob.text: Then I looked[a], rose up, and said to the nobles, to the officials, and to the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and fearsome, and fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives[b], and your houses.”

spob.text: I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “There is a great deal of work, and it is spread out over a wide area. We are separated along the wall, far from one another.”

pob.text: And I said to them[a], “The gates of Jerusalem must not be opened until the sun is hot. While they are still standing guard, let them shut the doors and fasten them. And appoint guards from the inhabitants of Jerusalem[c][b], each at his watch and each opposite his own house.”

pob.text: And they found it written in the Law that Yahweh had commanded through Moses that the sons of Israel should dwell in booths during the feast[a], in the seventh month.

spob.text: They found this written in the Law: Yahweh had commanded through Moses that the sons of Israel[a] were to live in temporary shelters during the festival in the seventh month.

public_domain_references.bsb: And they found written in the Law, which the LORD had commanded through Moses, that the Israelites were to dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month.

public_domain_references.asv: And they found written in the law, how that Jehovah had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month;

public_domain_references.brenton: And they found written in the law which the Lord commanded Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths, in the feast in the seventh month:

pob.text: and that they should proclaim and spread the message through all their cities and in Jerusalem[a], saying, “Go out to the hill country and bring branches of olive, oil tree, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees, to make booths[b], as it is written.”

spob.text: They were also to announce this message throughout all their cities and in Jerusalem: “Go into the hill country and bring back branches[b] from olive trees, oil trees,[a] myrtles, palms, and other leafy trees. Use them to build booths—temporary shelters—as it is written.”

public_domain_references.bsb: So they proclaimed this message and spread it throughout their towns and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the hill country and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written.”
public_domain_references.web: and that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters, as it is written.”

And Esdras said, Go forth to the mountain, and bring branches of olive, and branches of cypress trees, and branches of myrtle, and branches of palm trees, and branches of [every] thick tree, to make booths, according to that which was written.

pob.text: So the people went out and brought them[a], and made booths for themselves, each on his roof, and in their courtyards, and in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the square of the Water Gate[b], and in the square of the Gate of Ephraim.

spob.text: So the people went out and brought the branches. They made temporary festival shelters, called booths, for themselves. Each person made them on their own rooftop or in their courtyard, in the courtyards of God’s house, and in the public squares at the Water Gate and the Gate of Ephraim.

public_domain_references.asv: So the people went forth, and brought them, and made themselves booths, every one upon the roof of his house, and in their courts, and in the courts of the house of God, and in the broad place of the water gate, and in the broad place of the gate of Ephraim.

pob.text: And all the assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and lived in the booths[a], for the sons of Israel had not done so from the days of Jeshua son of Nun until that day. And there was very great rejoicing.

spob.text: Everyone in the gathered community who had returned from captivity made temporary shelters and lived in them. The sons of Israel had not celebrated the feast in this way since the days of Jeshua son of Nun.[a] There was very great rejoicing.

public_domain_references.bsb: The whole assembly who had returned from exile made booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the Israelites had not celebrated like this. And there was great rejoicing.
public_domain_references.web: All the assembly of those who had come back out of the captivity made temporary shelters and lived in the temporary shelters, for since the days of Joshua the son of Nun to that day the children of Israel had not done so. There was very great gladness.
public_domain_references.asv: And all the assembly of them that were come again out of the captivity made booths, and dwelt in the booths: for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.
public_domain_references.kjv: And all the congregation of them that were come again out of the captivity made booths, and sat under the booths: for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so. And there was very great gladness.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the congregation who had returned from the captivity, made booths, and dwelt in booths: for the children of Israel [had] not done so from the days of Jesus the son of Naue until that day: and there was great joy.

pob.text: And he read from the Book of the Law of God day by day[a], from the first day to the last day. And they kept the feast seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly[c][b], according to the ordinance.

spob.text: He read aloud from the Book of God’s Law every day, from the first day of the festival to the last. The people celebrated the festival for seven days. On the eighth day, they gathered for the prescribed solemn assembly.

public_domain_references.brenton: And [Esdras] read in the book of the law of God daily, from the first day even to the last day: and they kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.

pob.text: On the twenty-fourth day of this month[a], the sons of Israel assembled with fasting, in sackcloth[b], and with dirt on them.

spob.text: On the twenty-fourth day of this month, the Israelites[a] gathered together. They fasted, wore rough clothes made from sackcloth, and put dirt on themselves.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: On the twenty-fourth day of the same month, the Israelites gathered together, fasting and wearing sackcloth, with dust on their heads.

public_domain_references.kjv: Now in the twenty and fourth day of this month the children of Israel were assembled with fasting, and with sackclothes, and earth upon them.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month the children of Israel assembled with fasting, and in sackcloths, and with ashes on their head.

pob.text: Then the offspring of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners[b][a], and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

spob.text: Then the descendants of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners. They stood and confessed their own sins and the wrongs committed by their ancestors.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all the foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
public_domain_references.web: The offspring of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners and stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
public_domain_references.asv: And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all foreigners, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the children of Israel separated themselves from every stranger, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.

pob.text: And they stood in their place[a], and they read from the Book of the Law of Yahweh their God for a fourth of the day[b]; and for another fourth they were confessing and bowing down to Yahweh their God.

spob.text: They stood in their places.[a] For one quarter of the day, they read from the Book of the Law of Yahweh their God. Then they spent another quarter of the day confessing and bowing down to Yahweh their God.

public_domain_references.bsb: While they stood in their places, they read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day, and they spent another quarter of the day in confession and worship of the LORD their God.
public_domain_references.web: They stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of Yahweh their God a fourth part of the day; and a fourth part they confessed and worshiped Yahweh their God.
public_domain_references.asv: And they stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of Jehovah their God a fourth part of the day; and [another] fourth part they confessed, and worshipped Jehovah their God.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of the LORD their God [one] fourth part of the day; and [another] fourth part they confessed, and worshipped the LORD their God.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they stood in their place, and read in the book of the law of the Lord their god: and they confessed [their sins] to the Lord, and worshipped the Lord their God.

pob.text: Then Jeshua[a], Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Kenani stood on the platform of the Levites, and they cried out with a loud voice to Yahweh their God.

spob.text: Then Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Kenani stood on the platform used by the Levites.[a] They cried out loudly to Yahweh their God.

public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then stood up upon the stairs, of the Levites, Jeshua, and Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, [and] Chenani, and cried with a loud voice unto the LORD their God.

pob.text: Then the Levites—Jeshua[a], Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said, “Stand up; bless Yahweh your God from everlasting to everlasting. Blessed be your glorious name[b], which is exalted above all blessing and praise.”

spob.text: Then the Levites—Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said, “Stand up and bless Yahweh your God forever and ever! May your glorious name be blessed.[a] It stands above every blessing and praise.”

public_domain_references.web: Then the Levites, Jeshua, and Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah, said, “Stand up and bless Yahweh your God from everlasting to everlasting! Blessed be your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise!

public_domain_references.brenton: And the Levites, Jesus and Cadmiel, said, Rise up, bless the Lord our God forever and ever: and let them bless thy glorious name, and exalt it with all blessing and praise.

pob.text: You alone are Yahweh[a]. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them; and you preserve all of them alive[c][b], and the host of heaven bows down to you.

spob.text: You alone are Yahweh. You made the heavens, even the highest heavens, and all their heavenly host.[a] You made the earth and everything on it, and the seas and everything in them. You keep them all alive, and the heavenly host bows down to you.

public_domain_references.bsb: You alone are the LORD. You created the heavens, the highest heavens with all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them. You give life to all things, and the host of heaven worships You.
public_domain_references.web: You are Yahweh, even you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their army, the earth and all things that are on it, the seas and all that is in them, and you preserve them all. The army of heaven worships you.

public_domain_references.kjv: Thou, [even] thou, [art] LORD alone; thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth, and all [things] that [are] therein, the seas, and all that [is] therein, and thou preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Esdras said, Thou art the only true Lord; thou madest the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, and all their array, the earth, and all things that are in it, the seas, and all things in them; and thou quickenest all things, and the hosts of heaven worship thee.

pob.text: You are Yahweh God[a], who chose Abram, brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans, and gave him the name Abraham.

public_domain_references.asv: Thou art Jehovah the God, who didst choose Abram, and broughtest him forth out of Ur of the Chaldees, and gavest him the name of Abraham,
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou [art] the LORD the God, who didst choose Abram, and broughtest him forth out of Ur of the Chaldees, and gavest him the name of Abraham;
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou art the Lord God, thou didst choose Abram, and broughtest him out of the land of the Chaldeans, and gavest him the name of Abraam:

pob.text: You found his heart faithful before you[a], and made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, and the Girgashite—to give it to his offspring. And you have fulfilled your words[c][b], for you are righteous.

spob.text: You found that he was faithful to you in his heart. You made a covenant with him, promising to give his offspring[a] the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites. You have done what you said you would do, because you are righteous.[b]

You have kept Your promise, because You are righteous.

pob.text: You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt[a], and you heard their cry at the Red Sea.

public_domain_references.brenton: And thou sawest the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and thou heardest their cry at the Red Sea.

pob.text: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh[a], against all his servants, and against all the people of his land, for you knew that they acted presumptuously against them. So you made a name for yourself, as it is to this day.

spob.text: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all the people of his land because you knew they had acted arrogantly against them. So you made yourself famous, and your fame continues to this day.

public_domain_references.bsb: You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his officials, and all the people of his land, for You knew they had acted with arrogance against our fathers. You made a name for Yourself that endures to this day.

pob.text: You split the sea before them[a], and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry ground[b]; and you threw their pursuers into the depths like a stone in mighty waters.

pob.text: By a pillar of cloud you led them by day[a], and by a pillar of fire by night to give them light on the way in which they should go.

pob.text: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven[a], and you gave them upright judgments, true laws[c][b], good statutes and commandments.

pob.text: You made your holy Sabbath known to them[b][a], and you commanded them commandments and statutes and a law by the hand of Moses your servant.

spob.text: You made your holy Sabbath known to them. Through Moses your servant, you commanded them to follow your commandments, statutes, and law.[a]

pob.text: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger[a], and you brought out water from the rock for their thirst, and you told them to go in to possess the land that you had sworn to give them.

spob.text: You gave them bread from heaven when they were hungry and brought water out of the rock when they were thirsty. You told them to enter and take possession of the land that you had lifted up your hand in an oath to give them.
